Hello, I’m GPTREI, your requirements elicitation assistant. I’ll be gathering detailed information about the Unified University Inventory System to understand the needs clearly and support development effectively.

Before we begin, are you aligned with this interview scope, or do you have different expectations for what we should cover?

Yes, that scope sounds right to me. We want to focus on how the three faculties’ inventories get unified, who can view and manage what, and how requests and reservations should move through approval. If there are gaps, I can help clarify the day-to-day workflows and the practical access rules we need.
Thank you. To start off, could you please introduce yourself and your connection to this project?

I’m one of the university stakeholders involved in the inventory process, representing the operational side of how assets are managed across faculties and departments. I work with the people who handle rooms, equipment, and software licences, so I can speak to the current pain points and the way we need the unified system to support staff and approvals.
To help me understand the current situation, could you describe the current process or systems you use for managing rooms, equipment, and software licences across the three faculties?

Right now, each faculty mostly keeps its own inventory records, and they aren’t fully consistent with each other. Some things are tracked in spreadsheets or local databases, and approvals for room bookings or equipment requests are handled partly by email or manual forms. That makes it hard to get a single reliable view of what’s available across the university.
What current processes do you want to change or improve, or what main features do you hope to get from this unified inventory project?

We mainly want one shared system instead of three separate ones, so staff can see accurate inventory across the university in one place. We also want a proper request and approval workflow for assets and room reservations, with clearer responsibility at the university, faculty, or department level. It would also help if updates are immediate and people can trust that what they see reflects the real status.

So far, I understand the main features/functions as: a single shared inventory across the three faculties, role-based visibility and management at university/faculty/department levels, and a request-and-approval workflow for assets and room reservations with up-to-date status information.

Are there any other features you would like to see in this project?

Yes, a few things would be very useful, like search and filtering so staff can quickly find items or rooms, and reporting so we can see usage, shortages, and what needs renewal or replacement. It would also help to have audit trails for changes and approvals, since we need accountability. If possible, notifications for request status changes would be valuable too.
Based on your description, do you think integration with the existing faculty databases or tools should also be included?

Yes, definitely. We’d prefer the system to integrate with the existing faculty databases rather than require everyone to re-enter everything manually, because that would be too much work and error-prone. If some other tools are already being used for authentication or scheduling, it would make sense to connect to those too, but I’d need to check exactly which ones are in scope.

Great. To make sure I’ve captured the main feature set correctly, could you confirm whether these are the core features we should include: unified inventory data, role-based access, request and approval workflows, search and filtering, reporting, audit trails, notifications, and integration with existing databases and possibly authentication or scheduling tools?

Yes, that sounds like the core set we should be working with. The only thing I’d add is that the integration with authentication or scheduling tools is a “if feasible” item for now, because we may need to confirm what systems the university already has and what technical constraints there are. Otherwise, that list matches what we need.
Which of these core features would you prioritize first for the initial release?

For the first release, I’d prioritize the unified inventory data, role-based access, and the request and approval workflow, because those are the foundation of the whole system. Search and filtering should come next so staff can actually use the system efficiently. Reporting, audit trails, notifications, and integrations would be important too, but I’d see those as slightly secondary if we need to phase delivery.
For the unified inventory feature, what specific kinds of assets and records need to be included in the shared inventory from the start?

At minimum, we need rooms, equipment, and software licences in the shared inventory from the start. For each of those, we’d want the usual identifying and status details, like location or department, availability, condition, and who is responsible for it. If there are other asset types already tracked by one of the faculties, we can consider them later, but those three are the main ones.
Please elaborate on what you want this unified inventory to accomplish for rooms, equipment, and software licences.

For rooms, the system should let staff see availability, reserve them, and route those reservations for approval where needed. For equipment, we want to track who has it, whether it’s available or under maintenance, and allow requests for borrowing or assignment. For software licences, the main goal is to know what licences we have, how many are in use, and whether more can be allocated without going over the limit.
Could you describe the approval path you want for room reservations and asset requests, especially who should approve at the university, faculty, or department level?

The approval should follow the level that owns the resource. If it’s a department-owned item or room, the department admin should approve first; if it’s faculty-wide, then the faculty admin; and if it affects shared university resources, then it should go to the university level. I’d also expect some cases to need more than one approval step if the request crosses levels, but I’d need to confirm the exact rules with the administrators.
How should the request workflow behave after a user submits a room reservation or asset request—what statuses and notifications do you want along the way?

After submission, the request should move to something like pending review, then approved or rejected, and finally fulfilled or completed once the room or asset is actually assigned. If more information is needed, it should be put on hold or returned to the requester for revision rather than just rejected immediately. Notifications should go to the requester at each major change, and also to the next approver in the chain when action is needed.
What should staff at the university, faculty, and department levels be able to do versus only view in the system?

Staff who are responsible for inventory should be able to create, edit, and retire records within their own scope, and they should also process approvals and manage allocations. Ordinary users should mostly be able to search, view availability, and submit requests, but not change inventory records directly. University-level staff would need visibility across everything, while faculty and department staff should mainly manage what belongs to their own area, unless they’ve been given broader authority.
How detailed do you want the search and filtering to be for staff looking for items or rooms?

It should be detailed enough that staff can narrow results by location, department or faculty, availability, asset type, and status. For rooms, filters like capacity and time slot would be very helpful, and for equipment, condition or whether it is available for loan would matter. It doesn’t need to be overly complex in the first release, but it should quickly get someone to the right asset without a lot of manual checking.
What kinds of reports do you need the system to produce for inventory usage, shortages, and renewal or replacement planning?

We’d want regular reports showing what assets are most used, what is sitting unused, and where there are shortages or repeated requests that we can’t fulfill. For software licences, a renewal report should show expiry dates, current usage, and any licence types that are close to running out. For equipment and rooms, it would help to have replacement or maintenance planning reports that flag items in poor condition, overbooked spaces, or assets due for review.
How far back do you need the audit trail to record changes, approvals, and status updates in this system?

Ideally, we’d keep the audit trail for as long as the record exists, and probably longer if university policy requires it. At minimum, it should capture who changed what, when it changed, and what the previous value was, especially for approvals and status changes. I’m not sure yet whether there’s a formal retention period beyond that, so I’d need to check the university records policy.
Who else do you think has valuable insights into the project, and whose needs need to be considered, and why?

The main people to involve would be faculty administrators, department admins, IT staff, and the people who actually request rooms or assets. Faculty and department staff know the day-to-day approval and inventory pain points, while IT can help with security, integration, and access control. We should also include finance or procurement if licence renewals and replacement planning are part of the workflow, because they’ll care about budgets and lifecycle tracking.
What would you consider a successful deployment of this system, in practical terms?

A successful deployment would mean all three faculty inventories are merged accurately, staff can access the right information securely, and requests are moving through approval without confusion or delays. In practical terms, users should be able to find and reserve what they need, administrators should have clear visibility and control, and the old manual tracking should drop significantly. If people stop keeping separate spreadsheets and the reports are trustworthy, I’d consider that a strong success.

To summarize, we discussed a unified inventory for rooms, equipment, and software licences; role-based access by university, faculty, and department; request and approval workflows with statuses and notifications; search and filtering; reporting; audit trails; and integration with existing systems if feasible. Is there anything else you would like to add?

One thing I’d add is that the system should handle exceptions clearly, like when an asset is damaged, lost, under maintenance, or temporarily unavailable. It would also be useful if notifications could go to email at a minimum, since staff rely on that heavily. Other than that, I think you’ve covered the main needs pretty well.

Thank you for your valuable insights. We will follow up with any additional questions or clarifications needed. Based on our discussion, I will prepare a detailed summary and share it with you for review.
That sounds good. I’ll review the summary once you send it and let you know if anything needs correcting or clarifying.
